findings.body:
Removal of the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check plus the unconditional `urllib.request.urlopen(url, ...)` allows any caller-supplied URL to be fetched. If `deliver` is reachable with attacker-controlled `url` values (or even customer-controlled values that later become attacker-controlled), this enables SSRF to internal hosts, token exfiltration, or port scanning.

```suggestion
    host = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname or ""
    if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
        raise ValueError("webhook host not allowed")
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json_dumps(event), method="POST")
```

summary: The change removes the only host allow-list that guarded webhook delivery and replaces it with an unconditional `urlopen` on caller-supplied URLs. The stated motivation is customer-configured endpoints, but the implementation introduces an SSRF / data-exfiltration vector with no compensating control visible in the diff or the file.

verification.reason: Base had an ALLOWED_HOSTS check before urlopen; head removed it and posts to any caller-supplied URL, which is a real SSRF regression consistent with critical severity.
